g.text: Rendered evidence from captured output
Observed at +0.474719762802124s — page 17
```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PUT \
"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1" \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"tokens": { "sensitive_value": "[REDACTED]"$ACCESS_TOKEN"'", "expires_in": 3600 },
"clientInformation": { "clientId": "'"$CLIENT_ID"'" }
Every answer is the account: its `id`, `name`, `kind`, `isDefault`,
`needsReconnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.
### Addressing an account
`{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is always
read as an id: it matches that account or answers `404`, and an upload to an
unknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.
A name no account has makes `PUT` create the account; on every other route it
answers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with both ids in
`details.accountIds`.
A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and
is at most 64 characters. One outside that rule, or one that is also a
well-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names are
unique on the server, ignoring case.
### What an upload stores
* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is your own label, and
replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name
for one test user.
* **Uploaded accounts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local
app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the account's owner
included. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.
* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in the project.** The body
takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,
`authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is
refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.
* **Each token field is at most 16 KB.**
* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads
a fresh token before each run, or when the issuer rejects our refreshes, a
stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an
expired account lists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next
upload restores it.
* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and server: 60, refilling at 120 an
hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.
### Who can upload
An API key acts as the person who created it, with all of that person's
access. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who
is not a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a
server shared with the project, accounts are project accounts: only a project
admin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.
### Running evals as an account
A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.
To run evals from CI as one account, upload its token, make it the default,
then start the run:
